records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length (0x80) BER sequences, causing readSequence() to return an empty list instead of rejecting the malformed encoding
records.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readLength(), when the length octet is 0x80 it explicitly returns -1 to represent indefinite-length encoding (`if (length == 0x80) { return -1; }`). In readSequence(), the returned length is used directly in `while (length > 0) { ... }`, so a length of -1 skips the loop and returns an empty `List<byte[]>` without rejecting the encoding. This matches the finding: indefinite-length BER sequences are not rejected and lead to an empty list.
records.stripped_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length (0x80) BER sequences, causing readSequence() to return an empty list instead of rejecting the malformed encoding

records.issue_text: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) uses a dynamic string as format template with no arguments, causing UnknownFormatConversionException if a provider class name contains '%'; should be logger.debugf("%s", builder.toString())
records.rationale: In `common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java`, new code calls `logger.debugf(builder.toString());` where `debugf` treats its first parameter as a printf-style format string. Since `builder` includes provider class names (`foundProviders.get(i).getClass().getName()`), a class name containing `%` would be interpreted as a format specifier and can trigger `UnknownFormatConversionException`. Using `logger.debugf("%s", builder.toString())` (or `logger.debug(builder.toString())`) avoids this.
records.stripped_text: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) uses a dynamic string as format template with no arguments, causing UnknownFormatConversionException if a provider class name contains '%'; should be logger.debugf("%s", builder.toString())
